title: Why page sixteen sits beside page one

sources.B1: Adobe InDesign, Booklet types, section 2-up Saddle Stitch. https://helpx.adobe.com/indesign/desktop/print/print-booklets/booklet-types.html
sources.D1: Original worked example of the outside sheet of a 16-page left-bound booklet. Inspect the fold in the generated schematic. Artwork and sound generated for this example.

scenes.voice: Page sixteen, beside page one. Would you send this proof back?
scenes.picture: Outside sheet, flat on the table. The two page numbers come into view.
scenes.change: Viewer sees the pair that appears wrong.

scenes.voice: Watch the crease. One stays on the front. Sixteen folds behind it, onto the back.
scenes.picture: Keep the centre crease fixed as the left panel moves behind the right cover.
scenes.change: The flat print layout becomes a folded booklet.
scenes.sound: A brush of paper, then silence on the reveal.

scenes.voice: Open the booklet in the middle. Here, eight and nine really do belong side by side.
scenes.picture: Cut to the open centre spread. Reveal 8, then 9.
scenes.change: Reading order is visible at the centre.
scenes.sound: Quiet movement at the page turn.

scenes.voice: Now unfold the outside sheet again. Those two numbers were in the right place all along.
scenes.picture: Return to exactly the initial composition, now with front and back cover labels.
scenes.change: Viewer can identify both covers on the proof.
scenes.sound: A soft paper tap at rest.
